question: Will Gyanesh Kumar resign or be forced out of the position of Chief Election Commissioner of India by Oct 31, 2026?
outcomes: Yes - he will resign or be removed from his position as CEC
No - he will remain in his position as CEC

model.prompt_context:
Resolution criteria:
- "Yes - he will resign or be removed from his position as CEC": Wins if, on or before October 31, 2026 (UTC), Gyanesh Kumar has ceased to serve as Chief Election Commissioner of India as a result of a voluntary resignation, a presidential order of removal, a Supreme Court of India order, or any other official governmental action terminating his tenure before its scheduled end.
- "No - he will remain in his position as CEC": Wins if, as of the end of October 31, 2026 (UTC), Gyanesh Kumar continues to hold the office of Chief Election Commissioner of India and has neither resigned nor been removed.

Clarifications:
- A temporary leave of absence, recusal from a specific matter, or suspension pending proceedings does not constitute resignation or removal; only a formal, permanent departure from the CEC office qualifies.
- The official record of tenure status is established by notifications from India's Law Ministry or the President of India, or by a binding Supreme Court of India order.
